cohort_role: calibration — the second counter-pattern node. Inventorying it surfaced a real gap the audits had not recorded (see art-232.4-charge-type-outside-closed-set), which is the point of running the convention over nodes believed clean.
error_direction_rationale: The MAPR is tested against a 36% CAP (32 CFR 232.4(b)). Understating an included charge understates the MAPR and MISSES a violation at the cap — the harmful direction. Every resolved branch here therefore errs toward INCLUSION, and every unresolvable one returns 'conditional' rather than 'excluded'. The single exception is the unknown-charge-type fall-through, which returns null with no caveat, and that is recorded below as the node's one unrepresented branch precisely because it breaks this direction.

branches.branch: Any credit insurance premium or fee, single-premium credit insurance charge, debt cancellation contract fee, or debt suspension agreement fee is included in the MAPR.
Any fee for a credit-related ancillary product sold in connection with the transaction is included.
Finance charges associated with the consumer credit are included, subject only to the bona fide fee exclusion of (d), which reaches a fee OTHER THAN a periodic rate.

An application fee charged to a covered borrower is included, EXCEPT one charged by a Federal credit union or insured depository institution making a short-term small-amount loan, not more than once in any rolling 12-month period.
branches.note: The carve-out turns on three predicates this closed-set lookup does not collect — creditor class, loan terms, and the rolling-12-month history. Claiming it returns 'conditional' plus the predicates by name, never an 'excluded' verdict.

branches.branch: A participation fee is included subject to (c)(2)(ii)(B). On a credit card account a BONA FIDE participation fee may instead be excluded under (d)(1), and the $100-per-annum limit in (c)(2)(ii)(B) by its own terms does not apply to such a fee.

For a credit card account under an open-end (not home-secured) plan, a bona fide fee other than a periodic rate is excluded, but only to the extent it is bona fide and reasonable for that type of fee under the (d)(3) like-kind and safe-harbour standards.
branches.note: Reachability marker is included_in_mapr === 'conditional'. ⚠ That member is truthy on RESOLVED paths too, so it proves the refusal is reachable and does not, on its own, distinguish a caveat from an answer — the §2.2 mirror requirement is what would. Recorded rather than papered over.

branches.branch: The bona fide fee exclusion reaches credit card accounts only. Off a card, it cannot apply at all.

The bona fide fee exclusion does NOT apply to credit insurance premiums/fees, single-premium credit insurance, debt cancellation, debt suspension, or credit-related ancillary product fees — so a credit card account does not change the answer for those charges.
A charge in (c)(1)(i)-(iii) is included in the MAPR even where Regulation Z would exclude it from the finance charge.
Computing the MAPR itself — the Regulation Z APR rules for closed-end credit, the § 1026.14(c)-(d) effective-rate rules for open-end credit, and the no-balance billing-cycle rule.

assumption_of_use.owner: art-616, or the CALLER. This node classifies ONE charge for inclusion; it never computes a rate and never compares one to the 36% cap.

assumption_of_use.value: the 36% MAPR limit and the comparison against it
assumption_of_use.owner: the CALLER or a downstream node. Named here because the error direction of THIS node only matters relative to that cap.

branches.branch: A charge that is not one of the six charge_type values this closed-set lookup knows. The provision's chapeau reaches every charge 'as applicable to the extension of consumer credit'; the kernel's enumeration does not.
branches.note: ⛔ FINDING, surfaced by this inventory and NOT previously recorded. compute({charge_type:'late_fee'}) returns included_in_mapr:null, citation:null, basis:null, manual_review_required:false, and compliance_flags:['MLA_CHARGE_CLASSIFIED'] — a flag asserting the charge WAS classified when no branch matched. There is no refusal path: the if/else-if chain simply falls through. The harmful direction, because a caller reading a null inclusion as 'not included' understates the MAPR against a cap. ⛔ NOT FIXED HERE: adding the fall-through refusal moves the kernel digest and demands a re-prove in the same row (SO #36), which is outside this row's fence. Recorded for the ORCH to stage.
